sources.cite: CompTIA Project+ PK0-005 exam objectives: Project Management Concepts 33%, Project Life Cycle Phases 30%, Tools and Documentation 19%, Basics of IT and Governance 18%
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch of a training provider's syllabus page that restates the objectives in its own words (CompTIA's PDF on comptia.jp refused automated reading). Domains and weights as above. Relevant restated lines: change control (identify when a formal change request is needed; assess impacts on scope, schedule, cost, quality and risk; differentiate scope creep from approved change); meeting management (an agenda with timeboxes; attendees by decision rights; document decisions and action items); IT governance and change control (CAB/CCB; rollback readiness; post-change validation). The objective wording here is the course seed's; CompTIA's own wording is to verify.

sources.cite: Ken Schwaber and Jeff Sutherland, The Scrum Guide (November 2020)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 directly (the PDF). Daily Scrum: 'The purpose of the Daily Scrum is to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog as necessary'; 'a 15-minute event for the Developers of the Scrum Team'.

sources.cite: Ken Schwaber and Jeff Sutherland, The Scrum Guide (November 2020)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 directly (the PDF). Scrum Master accountabilities include 'Causing the removal of impediments to the Scrum Team's progress'; the Developers are accountable for 'Creating a plan for the Sprint, the Sprint Backlog' and 'Adapting their plan each day toward the Sprint Goal'.

sources.cite: Ken Schwaber and Jeff Sutherland, The Scrum Guide (November 2020)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 directly (the PDF). Definition of Done: 'If a Product Backlog item does not meet the Definition of Done, it cannot be released or even presented at the Sprint Review'; it returns to the Product Backlog for future consideration.

sources.cite: Ken Schwaber and Jeff Sutherland, The Scrum Guide (November 2020)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 directly (the PDF). Scrum values: 'Commitment, Focus, Openness, Respect, and Courage'; the three pillars transparency, inspection and adaptation; forecasts such as burn-downs 'do not replace the importance of empiricism'.

sources.cite: Ken Schwaber and Jeff Sutherland, The Scrum Guide (November 2020)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 directly (the PDF). Sprint Review: 'a working session and the Scrum Team should avoid limiting it to a presentation'; Retrospective: 'to plan ways to increase quality and effectiveness'.
